explanations.text: Her answer incorrectly attributes imbrication to the current pushing the flat side downstream, whereas the source describes that imbrication results when a rolling clast strikes a resting clast and the stalled clast tips until its long axis leans (i.e., dips) upstream as the bed rolls.

Her answer says the current pushes the flat side of each clast downstream, but source [2] explains that imbrication forms when a rolling clast stalls against a resting clast and tips until its long axis leans downstream, showing that the fabric records flow direction through clast‑to‑clast tipping, not by the current simply aligning flat sides.
